3.  Credit Card Purchasing Policy
  On February 6, 2018, the City of Avalon approved the Credit Card Purchasing Policy. The
  purpose of the policy is to establish a framework for the appropriate use of City-issued
  credit cards. The City reviews and updates existing policies on a periodic basis to ensure
  compliance with regulations and best practices.
  Recommended Action

4.  Authorize purchase of two (2) new Ford E-Transit vans for Dial-A-Ride service.
  The City of Avalon’s Dial-A-Ride service has been using two (2) 2015 Dodge Caravan
  minivans that were acquired in 2016. One of the vans has been inoperable for several
  months, and the other van has numerous maintenance issues. Both vehicles are beyond
  their useful life span, and not worth the cost to repair.
  Recommended Action
  1. Authorize City Manager, or their designee to procure, per the City’s purchasing policy,
  two (2) 2022 Ford E-Transit electric passenger vans for a total not to exceed $205,000 to
  be used for the City’s Dial-A-Ride service, and other transportation needs. 2. Amend the
  budget for the Avalon Transit Fund to include a $205,000 expenditure for Vehicle
  Replacement Fund (Account 12325-6781) and $164,000 in offsetting grant revenues
  (12325-8073) for a net increase of $41,000.

5.  Wastewater Treatment Plant Backup Generator Procurement
  On August 1, 2023, City Council authorized the City Manager or his designee to procure
  a used backup generator in accordance with the City’s procurement standards for a not
  to exceed cost of $85000, as a new unit would take approximately 12 months to procure.
  Since that time, Staff was able to locate and negotiate pricing for a new backup generator
  from Volvo Construction Equipment & Services.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the City Manager or his designee to procure a new backup generator from
  Volvo Construction Equipment & Services in accordance with the City’s procurement
  standards for a not to exceed cost of $100,000.

GENERAL BUSINESS

6.  Resolutions Adopting an Amendment to the Healthcare Article of the Memorandums of
  Understanding Between the City of Avalon and International Association of Firefighters
  Local 2295. Management, and Confidential/Unrepresented Labor Associations, and SEI U
  721 Avalon Harbor Unit and SEIU 721 Avalon Municipal Employee Unit
  The MOUs address City healthcare benefits by establishing a maximum contribution to
  be paid by the City toward the health care premium (“medical cap”). As it relates to
  healthcare benefits and cost of living increases, all MOUs contain a provision requiring
  parity between all associations. Under the medical cap outlined in the current MOUs, the
  increased premium rates will result in a significant increase to the out-of-pocket employee
  contribution since the commencement of the MOU’s. The proposed addendum replaces
  the two-tiered system with one and increases the medical caps by 4-20% depending on
  the plan type and hire date of the employee.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt resolutions amending the Healthcare Article of the Memorandums of
  Understanding between the City of Avalon and the International Association of
  Firefighters Local 2295, Management, Confidential/Unrepresented Associations, and

  SEIU 721 Avalon Harbor and SEIU 721 Avalon Municipal Employee Unions for the
  contract period July 1, 2022 through June 30. 2025.

7.  Award Above Ground Fuel Tank Foundation and Retaining Wall Contract
  As the second procurement component of this project, on August 11, 2023 the City
  solicited bids by informal bid process from duly licensed and experienced contractors to
  provide site preparation, grading, concrete foundation, retaining wall installation and
  related construction services for the new location of the storage tank. After an extension
  of the bid deadline, bidding closed on August 28, 2023 at 1 p.m. Only Jordahl
  Construction, Inc. provided a bid by the stated deadline.
  Recommended Action
  Make the determination the contract cost is reasonable and adopt a resolution by 4/5 vote
  awarding a contract to Jordahl Construction, Inc. for the site preparation, grading,
  concreate foundation and retaining wall installation for the City’s Underground Fuel Tank
  Replacement Project at a cost not to exceed sum of S301 000.

8.  Report Regarding Transient Rental License Findings
  On August 1, 2023, the City Council voted unanimously to establish, by urgency
  ordinance, a moratorium on the issuance of Transient Rental Licenses for transient rental
  use to new applicants for a 45-day period. The 45-day period expires on September 15,
  2023. Government Code standards require that at least 10 days before the expiration of
  the moratorium, the legislative body must issue a report describing the measures taken
  to alleviate the condition which led to the adoption of the ordinance.
  Recommended Action
  Receive and issue report. Provide direction to Staff.

ensure compliance with regulations and best practices.

acquisition period, reduce requests for employee reimbursements, and minimize the use of
personal credit cards for City-related expenses. In addition to the requirements outlined in the

and Expense Reimbursement Policy.

The Finance Department will continue to submit to City Council a supplemental report attached
to the bi-weekly warrant report describing the individual credit card transactions paid during the
period.

I.  Purpose

The purpose of the policy is to establish a framework for the appropriate use of City-issued credit cards.
The use of City-issued credit cards is intended to streamline small dollar purchases, reduce the
acquisition period, reduce requests for employee reimbursements, and minimize the use of personal
credit cards for City-related expenses. Employees with City-issued credit cards (Card Users) must also
adhere to the City’s Procurement Policy, as outlined in the Avalon Municipal Code, as well as the City’s
Travel and Expense Reimbursement Policy.

II.  Issuance of City Credit Card

Credit cards may be issued to City of Avalon department heads and their designees, as approved by the
City Manager. Credit cards shall not be issued to City Council Members, members of boards, committees,
or commissions, volunteers, part-time employees, seasonal employees, or contracted employees.

Prior to card issuance, employees will also be required to sign the cardholder agreement (Attachment A),
indicating that they understand and accept the terms of the policy.

The Finance Department is responsible for the activation, cancellation, and payment of City-issued credit
cards. Additionally, the Finance Director or their designee is responsible for the review of usage for
compliance with applicable purchasing policies.

IV.  Authorized Transactions

Purchases made by City-issued credit cards must adhere to the City’s Procurement Policy described in the
Avalon Municipal Code Title 3, Chapter 4 and the City’s Travel and Expense Reimbursement Policy.

V.  Unauthorized Transactions

The City credit card shall not be used for:
•  Cash advances:
•  Personal transactions unrelated to official City business;
•  Transactions beyond established credit limits;
•  Purchases that circumvent or violate City policies or exceed budgetary limits for the category of
  expense; and
•  Purchases unauthorized or unlawful under federal and state laws, including but not limited to
  ethical rules related to gifts and reporting obligations of eJected officials;

VI.  Reporting Requirements and Procedures

Within five business days of receiving the credit card statement, employees with City-issued credit cards
(Card User) must submit to the Finance Department detailed receipts and descriptions of all credit card
statement transactions, listing the business purpose1 attendees, date of purchase, merchant’s name and
budgeted account codes.

If for some reason the Card User does not have the proper documentation for a transaction, an explanation
shall be provided in the form of a memo countersigned by the Card User’s supervisor that includes a
description of the item, business purpose, attendees, date of purchase, merchant’s name, budgeted account
codes, and the reason why the documentation is missing.

Card Users shall take necessary measures to prevent unauthorized charges against the card. If the credit
card is lost or stolen, the Card User shall immediately report the occurrence to the Finance Director so that
the card may be cancelled. The Finance Department will coordinate with the Card User and the credit card
issuer in handling all disputed transactions.

If the credit card is used for personal transactions, such use shall be immediately reported and the amount
charged to the credit card shall be immediately refunded by the Card User.

VII.  Monitoring and Reporting

The Finance Department will submit to the City Council a supplemental report attached to the bi-weekly
warrant report that describes the individual credit card transactions for the month.

SUBJECT:  Authorize Purchase of Two (2) New Ford E-Transit Vans for Dial-A-
  Ride Services

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): 1. Authorize City Manager, or their designee to procure, per
the City’s purchasing policy, two (2) 2022 Ford E-Transit electric passenger vans for a total not
to exceed $205,000 to be used for the City’s Dial-A-Ride service, and other transportation
needs. 2. Amend the budget for the Avalon Transit Fund to include a $205,000 expenditure for
Vehicle Replacement Fund (Account 12325-6781) and $164,000 in offsetting grant revenues
(12325-8073) for a net increase of $41000.

REPORT SUMMARY: The City of Avalon’s Dial-A-Ride service has been using two (2) 2015
Dodge Caravan minivans that were acquired in 2016. One of the vans has been inoperable for
several months. and the other van has numerous maintenance issues. Both vehicles are
beyond their useful life span, and not worth the cost to repair. Having only one minivan in
service has created a hardship for Transportation Concepts, and the Dial-A-Ride service.
Numerous scheduled pickups have been cancelled while the one van has been out of service
for repairs.

Due to the availability of zero-emission vehicle (ZEV) grant funds from Metro, the City plans to
replace the minivans with all-electric Ford E-Transit passenger vans. The grant funds will cover
the entire cost of the vans. The versatility of these vans will allow us to use them for
transportation needs other than the Dial-A-Ride service if needed. One of the vans we are
looking to acquire was delivered to Avalon to allow staff from the City and Transportation
Concepts test drive the vehicle. Staff agreed these vans would be suitable for our
transportation needs. Being an all-electric vehicle also helps promote the goal to eventually
electrify all vehicles in our community.

The procurement of these vans would go through the City’s contract with HGACBuy, which is a
government cooperative procurement service. All contracts available to participating members
of HGACBuy have been awarded by virtue of a public competitive procurement process
compliant with state statutes. This fulfills our procurement requirements for Cooperative
Purchases within the Avalon Municipal Code.

FISCAL IMPACTS: Amend the budget for the Avalon Transit Fund to include a $205,000
expenditure for the Vehicle Replacement Fund (Account 12325-6781) and $164,000 in
offsetting grant revenues (12325-8073)fora net increase of $41,000.
 CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: Transportation
Concepts will continue to use the current inefficient minivan, which may continue to cause
cancellations of our Dial-A-Ride service.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Complete the vehicle procurement following the City’s purchasing
policy.

generator at the City’s Wastewater Treatment Plant was non-operable.

it would be inefficient or impossible to facilitate repairs. Staff determined a replacement should
be procured as soon as possible. A dependable primary and backup power source are essential
to the function of the wastewater treatment facility. As a temporary stopgap measure, Staff
located a rental portable generator for the facility to utilize. The cost of the rental is $6,300 per
month regardless of whether the generator is in use or not.

Ultimately, the generator is essential for operation and due for replacement. This expenditure is
budgeted in the wastewater treatment plant capital improvement plan.

On August 1, 2023 City Council authorized the City Manager or his designee to procure a used
backup generator in accordance with the City’s procurement standards for a not to exceed cost
of $85,000, as a new unit would take approximately 12 months to procure. Since then staff was
able to located and negotiate pricing for a new backup generator for a base price of $94,380
from Volvo Construction Equipment & Services located on Corona, CA. They have the generator
in stock, and would be available to us within a week. Additional funds are being requested to
allow City Manager to procure the new generator at a total cost not to exceed $100,000.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City will continue
to incur monthly rental inspections for a backup generator at the wastewater treatment facility
while a permanent solution is identified and implemented.

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Adopt resolutions amending the Healthcare Article of the
Memorandums of Understanding between the City of Avalon and the International
Association of Firefighters Local 2295, Management, Confidential/Unrepresented
Associations, and SEIU 721 Avalon Harbor and SEIU 721 Avalon Municipal Employee
Unions for the contract period July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2025.

REPORT SUMMARY: On May 3, 2022, City Council adopted resolutions approving the
Memorandums of Understanding (MOUs) between the City of Avalon and the International
Association of Firefighters Local 2295 (Resolution 22-25) Management Association
(Resolution 22-27), and Confidential/Unrepresented Association (Resolution 22-26)
effective July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2025.

On July 19, 2022, City Council adopted resolutions approving the MOUs between the City
and SEIU 721 Avalon Harbor Union (Resolution 22-43) and SEIU 721 Avalon Municipal
Employee Union (Resolution 22-44).

The MOUs address City healthcare benefits by establishing a maximum contribution to be
paid by the City toward the health care premium of the employee’s selected Plan (medical
cap”). As it relates to healthcare benefits and cost of living increases, all MOUs contain a
provision requiring parity between all associations. All MOUs tier the medical cap based on
employee’s date of hire.

Per the MOUs:

 Plan Type  Medical Cap  —  Medical Cap —

  Employee hired before 12131115  ,  Employee hired after 1/1/16
  Employee Only  $777.99  $667.69
I Employee+One  $1,283.21  $1,171.91
  Family  $1,600.00  S1,501.22

Employees may select healthcare plans that exceed the medical cap, but any excess costs
are paid by the employee (“out of pocket employee contribution”).
 Annually CaIPERs updates its member health benefits. CaIPERS healthcare plan premiums
increased approximately 12%-i 7% effective January 2023. In July 2023, City Staff received
the 2024 CaIPERs Association Premium update. The 2024 update showed an increase in
premiums by more than 15% over 2023 rates for some healthcare plans.

Under the medical cap outlined in the current MOUs, the increased premium rates will result
in a significant (as much as $6,000 a year) increase to the out-of-pocket employee
contribution since the commencement of the MOU’s.

The proposed addendum replaces the two-tiered system with one and increases the medical
caps by 4-20% depending on the plan type (employee only, employee +1 or family) and hire
date of the employee:

  Plan Type  Medical Cap  —

  Employee Only  $800.00
  Employee + One  $1,500.00
  Family  $1,875.00

Per the existing MOU agreements: ‘Any agreement, alteration, understanding, variation,
waiver or modification of any of the terms or provisions contained herein shall not be binding
upon the parties hereto unless made and executed in writing by all parties hereto, and
approve and implemented by Avalon’s City Council  For the life of this MOU, Union and
the City mutually agree that to reopen negotiations with respect to any subject or matter
covered in this MOU requires mutual consent by both parties...”

The City Manager presented a proposal to association and union representatives on August
17, 2023. There was consensus among the association/union representatives to move
forward with a formal amendment of the MOUs.

FISCAL IMPACTS: Potential increase to the FY 23-24 operations budget (account code
3045).

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Employee relations.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: Many employees
will have a significant increase to their out of pocket medical contribution.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Implement City Council direction.

ADVERTISING, NOTICE AND PUBLIC CONTACT: The item was properly listed on the
posted agenda pursuant to the Brown Act.

SUBJECT:  Award Above Ground Fuel Tank Foundation and Retaining Wall
  Contract

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Make the determination the contract cost is reasonable and
adopt a resolution by 4/5 vote awarding a contract to Jordahl Construction, Inc. for the site
preparation, grading, concreate foundation and retaining wail installation for the City’s
Underground Fuel Tank Replacement Project at a cost not to exceed sum of $301,000.

REPORT SUMMARY: The State of California requires the owners or operators of specific types
of underground fuel storage tanks to permanently close by December 31, 2025. The City of
Avalon owns four underground fuel tanks at the Avalon Fuel Dock that fall under this
requirement.

With assistance from former Assemblymember Patrick O’Donnell, the City was awarded a
$500,000 State budget earmark that is administered through the State of California Water Board
to remove the underground fuel tanks located at the fuel dock and install an above ground
system in compliance with the new regulations. The granting agreement requires the City to
have construction completed and the project closed out by June 30, 2024.

The project is included in the FY22-23 Budget and Capital Improvement Plan  —  Project Number
207004, Account Number 11470-6547 with $700,000 budgeted.
  —

On March 21, 2023 City Council approved the design and construction documents for this
project, and authorized Staff to post and receive informal bids to procure the fuel tank for an
amount not to exceed $200,000. On June 27, 2023, the City Council awarded a contract to
Western Pump fora not-to-exceed amount of $160,000.

As the second component of this project, on August 11, 2023 the City solicited bids by informal
bid process from duly licensed and experienced contractors to provide site preparation, grading,
concrete foundation, retaining wall installation and related construction services for the new
location of the storage tank. After an extension of the bid deadline, bidding closed on August28,
2023 at 1 p.m. Only Jordahl Construction, Inc. provided a bid of $274,710 by the stated deadline.

Unfortunately, in order to meet the informal bid procurement standards, the project sum cannot
exceed $200,000. Per the Procurement Policy as outlined in Avalon Municipal Code Section 3-
4.205 (b) (2): “If all bids received are in excess of the informal bidding limit, the Council may, by
adoption of a resolution by a 4/5 vote, award the contract, at or below the provisional limit set
forth in Public Contract Code § 22034(f), to the lowest responsible bidder, if it determines that
the Citys cost estimate was reasonable.”
 City Staff recommend the addition of a 10% contingency to the contract sum, and that City
Council make the determination the contract cost is reasonable and adopt a resolution by 4/5
vote awarding a contract to Jordahi Construction, Inc. for the site preparation, grading, concrete
foundation and retaining wall installation for the City’s Underground Fuel Tank Replacement
Project at a cost not to exceed sum of $301,000.

Time is of the essence as this project must have construction completed and project closed out
by June 30, 2024.

One procurement component of this project remains  —  removal of the underground storage tank,
site remediation and installation of the new tank.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: City Infrastructure. Reduction of high-risk facilities.

FISCAL IMPACTS: Total expenditure is not to exceed $301,000 towards CIP project code
207004 (account 11470-6547).

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City may not meet
the timeline required by the funding agreement with the State of California Water Board.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Execute an agreement with Jordahl Construction, Inc.

ADVERTISING, NOTICE AND PUBLIC CONTACT: This item was properly listed on the posted
agenda pursuant to the Brown Act.

SUBJECT:  Report Regarding Transient Rental License Findings

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Receive and issue report. Provide direction to Staff.

REPORT SUMMARY: On August 1, 2023, the City Council voted unanimously to establish, by
urgency ordinance a moratorium on the issuance of Transient Rental Licenses for transient
rental use to new applicants for a 45-day period. The 45-day period expires on September 15,
2023. Before considering any extension of the moratorium, the City Council must issue a
report that describes the measures taken to study and address the issues that lead to the
moratorium and what the City Council will due to address the issues of transient occupancy
licenses. This memo constitutes that report.

The moratorium was established to allow City Council, Planning Commission, City Staff and
the City Attorney time to study appropriate regulations to maintain public safety and health of
the community. Additionally, the moratorium temporarily halted further issuance of TRLs so
that the City can identify regulations which ensure that issuance of TRLs does not undermine
the City’s goals to have affordable housing stock and maintain a safe community.

Government Code standards require that at least 10 days before the expiration of the
moratorium, the legislative body must issue a report describing the measures taken to alleviate
the condition which led to the adoption of the ordinance.

Since the establishment of the moratorium, City Staff have held two stakeholder/community
meetings to discuss specific issues regarding transient rentals.
  -  On Tuesday, September 22 at 6 p.m. approximately 4 community members attended in
  person, with approximately 20 attending virtually. Meeting discussion included quality of
  life issues, specifically noise, trash, and other community impacts associated with
  transient rentals.
  -  On Wednesday, September 30 at 6 p.m. approximately 20 community members
  attended in person, with approximately 40 attending virtually. Meeting discussion
  included financial benefits and impacts, sustainability and housing impacts associated
  with transient rentals.

Staff compiled an extensive list of comments and regulatory options from community members
both in attendance at the meetings as well as those who provided written comments directly to
Staff.
 Additionally, City Staff have developed a community survey regarding transient rentals and
plan to circulate the survey on October 1, 2023, at the conclusion of the current income survey
period. The stakeholder/community meetings have helped Staff refine survey questions. Staff
anticipate circulating the survey for a 30-day period. Based upon the input from the community
meetings and responses to the survey, recommendations on future regulation of transient
rentals will be adopted.

As more analysis is needed, especially in light of the community survey, an extension of the
moratorium will allow issues associated with the impact of transient rentals on the health,
safety and welfare of city residents, the impact upon housing stock and city revenues, the City
Council has the option to extend the moratorium period.

A Public Hearing is scheduled for Friday, September 15 at 10a.m. regarding the consideration
of adoption of an ordinance extending the moratorium period on transient rental licenses.

FISCAL IMPACTS: None.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION:  The Citys existing
rules for the granting of transient occupancy licenses will remain in place.
